metric_rationale: Calculates the proportion of trials where the subject's choice matches the prediction of the Take The Best (TTB) heuristic. Because the experimental design explicitly pits TTB against Tallying on every single trial (the option that wins on the highest-validity discriminating cue always loses on the sheer number of winning cues), TTB will score near 1.0 on this metric, whereas Tallying will score near 0.0. The large mean difference and low within-theory variance make it a highly discriminative metric.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that are consistent with the Tallying heuristic on trials where Tallying has a strict preference (i.e., one option has more winning features than the other). In the chosen experimental design, these trials are exactly the ones designed to cause a strict preference reversal between Tallying and Take The Best (TTB). Because TTB predicts the exact opposite choice on these trials, data simulated under Tallying will yield a metric value close to 1.0 (subject to noise), whereas data simulated under TTB will yield a value close to 0.0. This creates a massive, reliable gap between the two theories.

The experimental design creates a perfect dissociation between WADD and Tallying. WADD strongly prefers Option A on trials 2, 3, 5, and 6, but strongly prefers Option B on trials 1 and 4. Tallying exhibits the opposite pattern: it prefers B on 3, 5, and 6, prefers A on 4, and ties on 1 and 2. By computing the difference in the proportion of A choices between the 'WADD-pro-A' trials and the 'WADD-anti-A' trials, we expect WADD to yield a score close to 1.0, while Tallying will yield a negative score (around -0.625). This large gap ensures robust discrimination between the two theories.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Tallying heuristic's predictions on all trials where Tallying has a strict preference. The experimental design specifically pits Tallying against WADD by creating trials where one option wins on a majority of features (favored by Tallying) but the other option has a massive cardinal advantage on a few high-validity features (favored by WADD). Consequently, this metric will be close to 1.0 for agents using Tallying and much lower (often below 0.5) for agents using WADD.
